reviewMethod: Exact named OpenStreetMap feature, official operator or destination page, and a destination-specific licensed campaign photograph.

north-point-lighthouse.name: North Point Lighthouse
north-point-lighthouse.summary: North Point Lighthouse is the separately operated museum and historic tower within Lake Park, reached from Wahl Avenue on the park's east side.
north-point-lighthouse.cost: Current admission is $8 for ages 12 and older, $5 for seniors, college students, and children ages 5-11, and free for children 4 and under, active military, and members; recheck before visiting.
north-point-lighthouse.hours: The museum and tower are normally open Saturday and Sunday from 1:00-4:00 p.m. The operator lists 2026 closures on April 5, July 4, July 25-26, and December 26; private events and later schedule changes can also override public hours.
north-point-lighthouse.needToKnow: The museum is accessible, but the tower is not: the climb includes 84 steps and a ladder. Tower climbers must be at least five years old and 38 inches tall. Admission and operating hours are separate from general park access.

lion-bridge.name: Lion Bridge
lion-bridge.summary: Lion Bridge is one of Lake Park's historic stone pedestrian bridges near North Point Lighthouse and the ravine trail network.
lion-bridge.cost: No separate admission is listed for this outdoor park landmark.
lion-bridge.hours: Outdoor access follows posted Lake Park hours and any temporary bridge, ravine, storm, or maintenance closure.
lion-bridge.needToKnow: Use the exact bridge pin or the official park map; the wooded ravines and multiple paths make the landmark easy to miss from the general park marker. Expect slopes and stairs on nearby routes.

veterans-park-lagoon.name: Veterans Park Lagoon
veterans-park-lagoon.summary: Veterans Park Lagoon is the sheltered water feature beside the lakefront lawn and the park's seasonal boat-rental operation.
veterans-park-lagoon.cost: Viewing and general park access are free; seasonal boat rentals are separately priced by the operator.
veterans-park-lagoon.hours: The lagoon is visible during park hours; boat rentals follow the seasonal operator schedule and can close for weather, water conditions, or low demand.
veterans-park-lagoon.needToKnow: Do not assume rentals are operating because the park is open. Check the current operator schedule before traveling specifically for a pedal boat, kayak, or other rental, and supervise children closely beside the water.

vilas-park-beach.name: Vilas Park Beach
vilas-park-beach.summary: Vilas Park Beach is the park's designated Lake Wingra swimming area at 1501 Vilas Park Drive, with seasonal restrooms and an accessible beach mat.
vilas-park-beach.cost: No separate beach admission is listed; parking limits and reservable facilities have separate rules.
vilas-park-beach.hours: The beach is unstaffed and has no lifeguard. Water quality is monitored during the maintained beach season, generally Memorial Day through Labor Day; restroom hours and services are seasonal.
vilas-park-beach.needToKnow: Check the city's beach status before swimming. The beach has no lifeguard, water conditions can change quickly, and nearby parking has a three-hour limit. The accessible mat is seasonal.

vilas-park-mound-group.name: Vilas Park Mound Group
vilas-park-mound-group.summary: Vilas Park Mound Group is a protected Indigenous burial-mound area within the park rather than a recreation surface or playground.
vilas-park-mound-group.cost: No separate admission is listed for respectful outdoor viewing from established paths.
vilas-park-mound-group.hours: The mound area can be viewed during open park hours unless a posted closure, restoration project, event, or weather condition restricts access.
vilas-park-mound-group.needToKnow: Remain on established paths and do not walk, sit, play, climb, bike, or place objects on the mounds. Treat the area as a protected burial site and follow all posted City of Madison rules.

millennium-park-beach.name: Millennium Park Beach
millennium-park-beach.summary: Millennium Park Beach is the staffed-season recreation area beside the six-acre beach and splashpad complex, separate from the park's free trails and open space.
millennium-park-beach.cost: Daily beach and splashpad admission is $4 for ages 16-62, $3 for ages 63 and older, $2 for ages 3-15, and free for ages 2 and under. Kent County says 2026 season-pass sales have ended; recheck future-season rates.
millennium-park-beach.hours: The beach is open 10:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. and splashpad 10:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. through August 23, then the beach closes at 7:00 p.m. and splashpad at 6:00 p.m. through Labor Day. The operator had not posted final 2026 closing dates when checked.
millennium-park-beach.needToKnow: Beach and splashpad admission is charged even though general park and trail access is free. Pets are prohibited in the beach area except trained service dogs. Use Lots A or B and verify same-day weather, water, and closing status before leaving.
